title: Things to do in Bergamo: 5 Upper Town sights
description: Things to do in Bergamo: five Upper Town sights, from Piazza Vecchia to the basilica, Rocca, Venetian walls and Citadel, with routes and access advice.
relatedQueries: what to see in Citta Alta Bergamo
intro: For a first visit to Bergamo, concentrate on five places in the Upper Town: Piazza Vecchia, the Basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore, the Rocca, the Venetian walls and the Visconti Citadel. Together they explain the city through civic squares, religious art and defensive architecture. You can organize the selection as a day of walking with breaks, choosing interiors according to their admission conditions and how much time you want to give them.

Important information checked on 9 November 2026: the Museo delle Storie announces that the Museo dell’Ottocento inside the Rocca remains closed for extraordinary maintenance following its closure on 8 September. Current visitor information distinguishes that museum from admission to the fortress’s Venetian tower, ramparts and terrace. This guide therefore recommends the Rocca without promising entry to the museum galleries or inventing a reopening date the operator has not announced.

sections.heading: 1. Piazza Vecchia: understand the city through its central square
paragraphs: Piazza Vecchia is a useful first stop for finding your bearings before entering a building. The Palazzo della Ragione, the Civic Tower known as the Campanone and, opposite, Palazzo Nuovo, home to the Angelo Mai Library, face the same space. The Contarini Fountain stands in the centre; official tourism information records its donation to the city in 1780. Change sides to see how the façades, arcades and fountain relate to one another. Each position reveals a different part of the ensemble.

The value of this stop is recognizing a place of government and gathering, rather than collecting admissions. Palazzo della Ragione helped define the separation between this space and present-day Piazza Duomo behind it. Use the passage between the two to appreciate the compact layout. The library, palace and Campanone have their own access arrangements: seeing them from the square does not include an interior visit or permission to climb the tower. Choose any of those additions after checking its particular calendar.

sections.heading: 2. Santa Maria Maggiore: begin with the lions’ porticoes
paragraphs: The Basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore belongs to the Piazza Duomo ensemble, but it should not be confused with the neighbouring cathedral. Its exterior is a worthwhile visit in itself: the entrances are lateral, and porticoes resting on lions mark two sides. The red lions face Piazza Duomo, while the white-lion portico faces Piazza Rosate. The photograph here shows a detail of that exterior. Walking around the building reveals reliefs and proportions that are easy to overlook when searching for a single frontal façade.

For entry, distinguish sightseeing from worship. The notice linked by Fondazione MIA establishes tourist admission with exemptions while keeping access for worship free; these are different arrangements. The consulted pages also do not present one identical tourist visiting period matching general opening, so check current instructions for your day. When the interior is available, it contains tapestries, wooden inlays associated with Lorenzo Lotto and Donizetti’s funeral monument. Staying outside is a valid choice, but it is different from seeing those works.

sections.heading: 3. Rocca: fortress views with the museum currently closed
paragraphs: The Rocca occupies Sant’Eufemia hill, an elevated part of the Upper Town. The operator dates the start of the present fortress to 1331 and its completion to 1336; later Venetian alterations introduced features including the substantial round tower. Parco delle Rimembranze surrounds the keep. The contrast with Piazza Vecchia is clear: here, the terrain and architecture explain control over the city. Views across roofs and the surrounding landscape depend on visibility, rather than any guaranteed panorama or a competition to collect observation points.

The closure notice concerns the Museo dell’Ottocento and should not automatically be interpreted as closure of the entire fortress. Current visitor information separately describes ticketed access to the Venetian tower, ramparts and panoramic terrace. Confirm which sections are operating before purchasing, and do not plan on museum galleries while maintenance continues. The operator warns of architectural barriers. Anyone needing a route without steps should ask about the particular spaces instead of assuming a neighbouring park guarantees tower access. Allow time for both the uphill approach and the return.

sections.heading: 4. Venetian walls: choose a section of the promenade
paragraphs: The walls enclose the Upper Town and explain its relationship with the landscape. Regional tourism information describes a sixteenth-century system extending for more than six kilometres, with four monumental gates, recognized by UNESCO in 2017 as part of the Venetian defensive heritage. A first visit does not require completing the perimeter. Choose a section of Viale delle Mura that fits your arrival or departure and notice the differences between a wall, a bastion and a gate. These features had different functions within the defences.

You can combine the walk with the surroundings of Porta San Giacomo or another entrance along your route. Follow public paths and areas open to visitors, using pauses to interpret the city’s edge, without assuming underground passages or enclosed structures are open. Museo delle Storie also operates a place called Mura di Bergamo with separate admission conditions; the exterior promenade does not include that museum. If rain or poor visibility makes the viewpoint less appealing, shorten this part and spend longer around the squares instead of trying to complete six kilometres as a requirement.

sections.heading: 5. Visconti Citadel: a courtyard with several layers of history
paragraphs: The Cittadella Viscontea reveals another way power was organized within Bergamo. This former Visconti fortified space became a characteristic Upper Town square. Visit Bergamo relates today’s courtyard to the Hospitium Magnum of 1379, which housed the military garrison. Approaching from the historic centre takes you beneath the Campanella tower. Then look across the whole space, its buildings and passages, rather than making the stop about one tower alone. The courtyard scale offers a different experience from the civic square and open wall promenade.

The complex houses the Civic Archaeological Museum and the Natural Science Museum, but their interiors are additional choices with opening calendars and admissions to check. This selection’s stop is the Citadel and its exterior. Adalbert’s Tower can be recognized from the square; official tourism information warns that it has no ground-floor entrance, so it should not be planned as a normal tower ascent. From this area, arrange your return towards Colle Aperto or back through the centre according to where you have planned the descent.

sections.heading: Reach the Upper Town and arrange the return
paragraphs: ATB distinguishes the city funicular connecting Lower and Upper Bergamo from the San Vigilio funicular, which is another service and a separate outing. For these five places, organize access to the Upper Town itself; a journey to San Vigilio is not assumed. If arriving from the railway station or BGY airport, the operator explains connections using the Airport Bus, route 1 and the city funicular, with routes and transfers depending on the service chosen.

Consult the journey planner, service notices and timetable for your date. ATB separates summer and winter calendars and publishes exceptions, so a general frequency should not be treated as a guarantee for the final return. Establish which zones and services a ticket covers before validating it. With luggage, allow a margin between the walk and a rail or air connection: reaching the Lower Town does not mean you are already at the station or airport.

sections.heading: Admission, slopes and choices that improve the visit
paragraphs: Begin the map with your arrival and departure points. From Colle Aperto, the Citadel can come before Piazza Vecchia; arriving from the other side may place the Rocca earlier. These are organizational options rather than compulsory circuits. Fit the basilica around tourist admission and the Rocca around the calendar for its open sections. A break between the two helps maintain a comfortable pace and decide which interior deserves your time.

Official tourism information describes cobbles and slopes on approaches to the basilica, while the Rocca operator warns of architectural barriers. Accessibility means checking the full journey, including level changes and return transport. The Milan, Padua and Lucca guides linked below help compare other Italian cities and interests. They represent other stages of a trip and should not all be treated as short excursions from Bergamo or as part of this walking route.

itinerary: With one day: choose your Upper Town arrival, connect the Citadel and Piazza Vecchia, and include the exterior of Santa Maria Maggiore. After a break, dedicate a block to the Rocca if its available sections interest you, then finish with a wall section that suits your return. Reverse the direction when arriving through another entrance.

With half a day: prioritize Piazza Vecchia and Santa Maria Maggiore, adding one extension: the Rocca, or the Citadel with part of the walls. Avoid interiors that force the walk into a rush. Do not keep the closed museum at the Rocca on a list of visits you hope to fit in later.

With more time: spread the five places across relaxed outings and add only interiors whose calendars you have confirmed. Save part of the visit for views when conditions suit them. During rain, give more time to art and interpretation inside buildings instead of trying to complete the entire defensive perimeter.

faq.question: Which five places should I see in Bergamo’s Upper Town?
faq.answer: Piazza Vecchia, the Basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore, the Rocca, the Venetian walls and the Visconti Citadel. Combine them on foot around your arrival point, the slopes and whichever interiors you choose.

faq.question: Is the Rocca’s Museo dell’Ottocento open?
faq.answer: Official information checked on 9 November 2026 retains the extraordinary maintenance closure that began on 8 September. The operator distinguishes the museum from the fortress tower, ramparts and terrace. Verify the available sections for your travel date.

faq.question: Is tourist entry to Santa Maria Maggiore free?
faq.answer: Fondazione MIA distinguishes paid tourist admission with exemptions from free access for worship. Check the current conditions for your intended visit rather than assuming general opening permits sightseeing at any time.

faq.question: Must I travel to San Vigilio for this route?
faq.answer: No. This selection concentrates on five places in the Upper Town. San Vigilio’s funicular serves another outing; Bergamo’s city funicular is the service connecting the Lower and Upper Towns.

conclusion: Bergamo rewards a route that alternates squares, details and landscape. Choose the arrival, check admissions that shape the day and allow time to look closely. These five places offer a flexible introduction to the Upper Town, with room to enjoy its architecture and adjust the visit when a particular part of a complex is unavailable.
